newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RESEARCH ALERT - U.S. rates rise to cool HK property.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - U.S. rates rise to cool HK property.

text.p: An expected rise of 0.75 percentage point in U.S. interest rates during 1997 should have a cooling effect on Hong Kong's overheated property market but limited impact on its economy, Hang Seng Bank said.

As local interest rates move in tandem with U.S. rates, the anticipated rate rise would restrain property prices and reduce the affordability of home purchase, the bank said in a research report released on Thursday.
Prices of flats in popular housing estates had gone up 37 percent from October 1995 to the last quarter of 1996, it said.
The affordability ratio -- the ratio of monthly mortgage repayment to median household income -- is currently close to its last peak in early 1994, it noted.
But a major correction in property prices seems unlikely because the interest rate rise is expected to be small, it said.
The report pointed out that there was little need for the U.S. Federal Reserve to raise interest rates by more than 75 basis points in 1997, judging from economic factors.
Such a moderate increase in interest rates would have only limited impact on Hong Kong's economy, it said.
